newsitem.title: USA: Intel to buy stake in Standard Micro.
newsitem.headline: Intel to buy stake in Standard Micro.

text.p: Intel Corp will make an equity investment in Standard Microsystems Corp, Standard Micro said Wednesday.
Standard Micro also said it projected a net loss for the fiscal fourth quarter of $1.22 to $1.29 a share.
It said that under a signed agreement, Intel will buy 1.54 million Standard Micro shares, representing just under a 10 percent interest, at a price of $9.50 per share.
Intel will also receive warrants to buy another 10 percent interest, as well as certain anti-dilutive rights, it said.
Standard Micro said it sees revenues for the fiscal fourth quarter ended February 28 totalling about $62 million, and for the full year $355 million.
The net loss for the year is expected to be $18.8-$19.8 million, or $1.36-$1.44 a share, it said.
First Call's consensus estimate is a break-even fourth quarter, and earnings of $0.05 a share for the year.
Standard Micro blamed the poor fourth quarter on lower revenues from its component products and system products divisions.
The components division was caught in an industry with excess semiconductor manufacturing capacity and a market with competitive prices, it said.
The system division also faced aggressive price competition, a LAN slowdown throughout the industry, and lower sales for older Ethernet products, it said.
Standard Mirco said a reduction in the carrying value of certain inventory to its net realizable value also hurt its gross profit for the fourth quarter by about $7 million.
It said it expected to take a charge to accrue the estimated cost of legal fees associated with litigations.
Severance costs associated with staff cutbacks and the accrual for legal fees decreased pre-tax earnings for the fourth quarter by about $2 million, it said.
Standard Micro said it would release its fourth quarter and full year results in April.
